workflow_steps.objective: Confirm the business goal, positioning challenge, audiences, brand name and language requirements, asset scope, constraints, approval roles, schedule, budget and success criteria.
Study the intended customers, dessert category, local competitors, venue context and relevant Chinese cultural and linguistic considerations without using the published reference as a style template.
Translate the agreed positioning into distinct design principles covering brand character, cultural specificity, modernity, accessibility, differentiation and practical use.
Define the identity architecture, Latin and Chinese naming hierarchy, required logo configurations, application priorities, formats, dimensions and production requirements.
Develop meaningfully different strategic identity directions, each demonstrating an original logo idea, typography, colour, graphic language and representative applications.
Evaluate the directions against the approved principles and obtain an explicit client decision on one direction and any elements to retain.
Resolve feedback within the selected direction, refine logo geometry and typography, validate bilingual relationships, and test legibility, scalability, contrast and distinctiveness.
Formalize the approved logo suite, typography, colour palette, graphic devices, imagery guidance, layout rules, accessibility guidance and usage governance.
Apply the approved system to the agreed parlour touchpoints and create representative mockups that demonstrate consistent real-world behavior.
Prepare technically valid vector, raster, print and digital masters with correct colour modes, sizing, exports, naming and licensing documentation.
Quality-check and package final assets, guidelines, application files and mockups; document contents and obtain final acceptance.

observations: The visible image is a wide landscape composition dominated by warm, dark-brown and beige tones.
A large circular object with closely spaced concentric ridges occupies much of the lower-central area.
Several pale rounded forms overlap the circular object, while hard-edged plant-like shadows cross the upper and right portions of the image.
A small, high-contrast white graphic is centered over the circular form and combines an elongated illustrated shape with separated lowercase Latin letterforms.
Small white typographic labels appear near all four corners; the upper-right label uses Chinese characters, while the other visible corner labels use Latin text.
The composition uses substantial dark negative space and strong tonal contrast between the photographic background, corner text and central white mark.

missing_inputs: Confirmed brand name, Chinese name, Latin spelling, pronunciation, descriptor and trademark status.
Business story, positioning, value proposition, desired attributes, price tier and measurable project goals.
Target customer segments, geographic market, venue format, service model and competitive set.
Required language variants, translation ownership, cultural references to embrace or avoid, and an authorized linguistic or cultural reviewer.
Menu architecture, hero products, dietary messaging and mandatory customer-facing copy.
Existing brand, interior, architectural, photographic or illustration assets and evidence of usage rights.
Exact application scope, such as storefront, menus, takeaway materials, tableware, uniforms, social templates or digital channels.
Dimensions, substrates, print methods, signage constraints, digital specifications and vendor requirements for scoped applications.
Accessibility requirements, budget, schedule, revision allowance, approval hierarchy and final decision-maker.
Required source-file formats, software compatibility, licensing expectations and handoff structure.
assumptions: The commission is for a new or substantially new identity rather than a minor update to an established system.
The business is primarily a customer-facing dessert parlour; packaged retail SKUs, merchandise and a full environmental program are excluded unless added to the agreed scope.
Both Chinese and Latin-script identity behavior may be required, but the precise language hierarchy remains subject to confirmation.
The published reference is evidence of the general deliverable family only and will not determine the new identity's visual direction.
Representative mockups will be used for evaluation, while editable production assets will be created only for applications explicitly approved in scope.
Final delivery is assumed to include scalable logo masters, standard digital exports and concise identity guidance, subject to confirmed technical requirements.
stop_conditions: Do not begin concept development until the brand name, core positioning, audience, language requirements and approval authority are confirmed.
Pause any naming or logo route that presents unresolved trademark, translation, cultural-sensitivity or misleading-claim risk until qualified review is obtained.
Do not merge or advance multiple directions without an explicit client selection and a documented list of accepted decisions.
Do not expand the system into applications until the core direction and logo have been approved.
Do not prepare production-ready application files without final copy, dimensions, substrates, vendor specifications and licensed assets or fonts.
Do not release final deliverables until technical QA, accessibility checks, licensing review and designated stakeholder approval are complete.
rationale: The request spans strategy, original concept development, system definition, application expansion and final handoff, so concept_to_production is more appropriate than a visual-exploration-only classification. The workflow uses explicit approval gates and treats the low-resolution reference solely as visible evidence of a completed identity presentation.
